name_note: GTDB places Eubacterium ramulus in g__Eubacterium_I, one of several genera split from the classical genus Eubacterium, so this group is narrower than Eubacterium as used in most papers.

sentences.text: Eubacterium ramulus is a human intestinal anaerobe known for its ability to degrade various dietary flavonoids.
It degrades quercetin, one of the most commonly consumed flavonoids, and a study reported that cross-feeding of sugars from starch by Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron stimulates its butyrate production.
Another study reported that it hydrogenates xanthohumol, a prenylated flavonoid found in hops and beer, and converts 8-prenylnaringenin into chalcones.
In stool metagenomes from 6419 FINRISK 2002 participants, the relative abundance of Eubacterium_I ramulus was inversely associated with incident pneumonia.
